external_entities.name: duty engineer
external_entities.description: An engineer who uses the dispatch console.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.
external_entities.notes: The text does not describe how an engineer signs in.

external_entities.name: scheduling partner
external_entities.description: Another company that publishes tomorrow's planned work.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company, publishes tomorrow's planned work.

processes.name: dispatch console
processes.description: A single-page JavaScript application opened by duty engineers in a browser.
processes.source_excerpt: The console is a single-page JavaScript app
processes.notes: The text does not state how engineers authenticate to the console.

processes.name: corporate web host
processes.description: The corporate web host that serves the dispatch console.
processes.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it

processes.name: dispatch API
processes.description: The API called by the dispatch console and schedule importer. It runs in the production control plane.
processes.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.
processes.notes: The control plane is not reachable from the internet.

processes.name: schedule importer
processes.description: A process that pulls the scheduling partner's SOAP feed, parses XML, archives downloaded documents, and posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API.
processes.source_excerpt: Our schedule importer runs on the corporate network.
processes.notes: The text does not say how the partner identifies the importer or how the importer identifies the partner. The API token has not been rotated since it was issued.

data_stores.name: dispatch database
data_stores.description: A database holding job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order.
data_stores.source_excerpt: That database holds the job orders, the crew names and the crew mobile numbers.
data_stores.notes: Every job order carries the token or session that created it, and nothing about the person behind that token. Protection at rest is not documented.

data_stores.name: schedule archive
data_stores.description: A folder on the corporate file store containing each document downloaded from the scheduling partner.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive, a folder on the corporate file store.

data_flows.name: open console
data_flows.description: A duty engineer opens the dispatch console in a browser.
data_flows.source_excerpt: They open the dispatch console in their browser.
data_flows.notes: The text does not state how the engineer signs in.

data_flows.name: serve app
data_flows.description: The corporate web host serves the dispatch console application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it

data_flows.name: call API
data_flows.description: The dispatch console calls the dispatch API cross-origin.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console calls the dispatch API.
data_flows.notes: The API answers the console cross-origin. Allowed origins and whether credentials are allowed were not recorded.

data_flows.name: stream status
data_flows.description: The dispatch console opens and holds a WebSocket to the dispatch API for live job status.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console also opens a WebSocket to the dispatch API and holds it open for live job status.
data_flows.notes: Whether the socket runs over TLS, whether its handshake is authenticated, and whether it checks the engineer's session again after opening were not recorded.

data_flows.name: read and write
data_flows.description: The dispatch API reads from and writes to the dispatch database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.data_description: job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and creating tokens or sessions

data_flows.name: pull feed
data_flows.description: The schedule importer pulls the scheduling partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS every hour.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every hour it pulls the partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS
data_flows.notes: How the partner identifies the importer and how the importer identifies the partner were not recorded.
data_flows.data_description: tomorrow's planned work in an XML document

data_flows.name: write documents
data_flows.description: The schedule importer writes downloaded documents into the schedule archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive
data_flows.data_description: downloaded XML documents containing planned work

data_flows.name: post work orders
data_flows.description: The schedule importer posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API using an API token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The importer then posts the parsed work orders to the same dispatch API the console calls.
data_flows.notes: The API token was issued when the importer was built and has not been rotated.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where duty engineers sit, the schedule importer runs, and the schedule archive is located.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: production control plane
trust_boundaries.description: The same-company zone holding the live estate, where an account can move a crew and change the work a depot does that day.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The control plane is the same company and the same staff, but it is the zone that holds the live estate
trust_boundaries.notes: The control plane is not reachable from the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: scheduling partner
trust_boundaries.description: The zone controlled by the scheduling partner, another company.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch database is in the production control plane because it is the data store used by the dispatch API running in that privileged zone.
assumptions.basis: The text places the dispatch API in the production control plane and describes the database as the API's read-write store, but does not explicitly locate the database.

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch database's classification is confidential because it contains crew names, crew mobile numbers, job orders, and token or session values.
assumptions.basis: The stated contents include personal contact information and authentication-related token or session values.

assumptions.assumption: The schedule archive's classification is business-sensitive and therefore confidential because it stores tomorrow's planned work.
assumptions.basis: The archive contains planned operational work documents, which are commercially sensitive business records.
